title: Hyperuniform systems are maximally irreversible
authors: Mathias Casiulis, Satyam Anand, Stefano Martiniani
abstract: Hyperuniform systems, defined by the anomalous suppression of large-scale density fluctuations, are a paradigm of non-equilibrium self-assembly. While mechanisms underlying the self-assembly of hyperuniform states have been widely studied, the energetics of this process remain unexplored. This raises a fundamental question: what is the energetic cost of self-assembling a hyperuniform system? Here, we address this question across several noisy particle systems drawn from soft matter and machine learning, in which hyperuniformity can be induced by tuning noise correlations. Despite their distinct microscopic dynamics, we uncover a universal behavior across all systems: hyperuniform states are maximally irreversible, as quantified by the entropy production rate. Further, we develop a path integral formulation of the entropy production rate directly from the microscopic dynamics, which explains our observations. Our work establishes a direct link between emergent long-range structure and time irreversibility and opens a new avenue of probing the energetic cost of hyperuniform self-assembly, ubiquitous across physics, biology, and materials science.
summary: The paper investigates the energetic cost of forming hyperuniform structures in various noisy particle systems. By calculating the Entropy Production Rate (EPR) using advanced path integral methods, the authors demonstrate a universal finding: these ordered states are maximally irreversible. This establishes a quantitative link between emergent long-range structure and time asymmetry.
main_problem: The study aims to determine the energetic cost associated with self-assembling hyperuniform systems and establish a fundamental link between emergent long-range structure and time irreversibility.
main_result: All studied noisy particle systems exhibit maximal time-irreversibility, quantified by the Entropy Production Rate (EPR), precisely when they achieve a hyperuniform state. This establishes a direct energetic cost for maintaining this ordered, non-equilibrium structure.
method: The authors combine numerical simulations with theoretical derivations, developing a path integral formulation to calculate the EPR directly from microscopic dynamics across various noise correlation structures.
model_or_system: The models include noisy particle systems drawn from soft matter and machine learning contexts (e.g., RO, SGD), covering both inter-particle spatial noise correlations and active bath temporal noise correlations.
key_observables: Hyperuniformity (suppression of large-scale density fluctuations); Entropy Production Rate (EPR or $\sigma(t)$); Correlation coefficients ($c_s$ for space, $c_t$ for time).
important_parameters: Noise correlation coefficients ($	ext{cs}, 	ext{ct}$), which tune the system from equilibrium towards non-equilibrium steady states (NESS).
main_assumptions: The analysis assumes that hyperuniformity can be induced by tuning noise correlations and focuses on quantifying the EPR as the measure of energetic cost.
figures_summary: Figures illustrate schematics for spatial noise systems (RO, BRO, SGD) and temporal noise systems in an active bath, setting up the physical models under investigation.
paper_structure: The paper progresses by first defining the problem—quantifying the energy cost of hyperuniformity. It then develops theoretical tools (path integral formulation for EPR) to analyze distinct noisy particle systems, culminating in the universal finding that maximal irreversibility coincides with hyperuniform structure.
why_interesting: This work provides a powerful, quantitative link between geometric order (long-range structure/hyperuniformity) and thermodynamic irreversibility ($	ext{EPR}$), which is highly relevant for understanding non-equilibrium steady states in complex physical systems.
